button.title: Button & IconButton
button.purpose: Triggers an action on the current surface (save, submit, open, delete). Navigation between pages is a link, not a Button.
use: Committing or cancelling a task (forms, dialogs, toolbars).
Icon-only actions in dense toolbars (IconButton + aria-label + Tooltip).
avoid: Choosing a filter, sort or scope → Chip (variant="advanced").
Switching views or sections → Segmented or Tabs.
Navigating to another page → a link or Sidebar item.
do: Give each surface exactly one Primary button, the main CTA.
Use Tertiary for every other action; it is the most common level.
Pair actions as Tertiary (dismiss) + Primary (commit), with Primary last, on the right.
Use Danger or Danger-Subtle for irreversible actions (Delete, Discard).
Start labels with a verb and keep them to 1–3 words ("Save changes", "Invite").
Disable a button only while its precondition is unmet, and explain why nearby (help text, validation).
Show progress on the button itself ("Deleting…") and disable siblings while it runs.
dont: Don't use Secondary as the default second button. It is a rare highlight (e.g. a pressed toolbar toggle); justify it with zen-allow-secondary.
Don't use Accent for ordinary primaries; reserve it for promoted CTAs (upsell, onboarding, the floating feedback action).
Don't put two Primary buttons side by side.
Don't use a Button to open a filter/sort list.
Don't ship an IconButton without aria-label.
Don't use vague labels ("OK", "Click here") for consequential actions.
a11y: Native <button>; Enter/Space activate. Focus ring is Focus/Accent (3px).
IconButton requires aria-label; add a Tooltip with the same text for sighted users.
Toggle buttons expose aria-pressed.
Minimum hit target 24px (2xs); prefer ≥ 32px (sm) for pointer, 40px (md) for touch.
content: Match the dialog title's verb in its primary action ("Delete project?" → "Delete project").

rules.summary: Secondary is a rare highlight; default to Primary (main CTA) or Tertiary.
Filter, sort and scope pickers are Chip (variant=advanced), never buttons.
Accent is for promoted CTAs (upsell, onboarding) only.
Irreversible actions (Delete, Remove, Discard) use Danger or Danger-Subtle.
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label.

chip.title: Chip / Pill
chip.purpose: Compact, selectable tokens. Advanced chips are the Zen filter control: each owns a Popover of options.
use: Filter/sort/scope/status/owner pickers (variant="advanced" + popoverItems).
Toggleable topic pills (variant="normal", aria-pressed).
Counts in dense layouts (variant="number-only").
do: Use one Advanced chip per filter dimension (Status, Owner, Date).
Show the chosen value as the chip label for single selection; show the counter for multiple.
Wire onClearSelection so Delete/Backspace and the × clear the filter.
Offer "Clear all" (Tertiary button) when two or more filters are active.
Keep Advanced chips' Popover open while toggling multiple options (popoverMultiple).
dont: Don't use Secondary or any Button to open a filter list.
Don't use Segmented to filter data (Segmented switches views).
Don't give a Normal or Number-only chip popoverItems.
Don't wrap chips inside another button.
a11y: Chip is a <button>; the Popover is a listbox with role=option items.
↓ opens, Escape closes and returns focus, Delete/Backspace clears (aria-keyshortcuts).
Topic pills expose aria-pressed.
content: Label the chip with the dimension ("Status") until a value is picked, then the value ("Done").

rules.summary: Filter, sort and scope pickers are Chip (variant=advanced), never buttons.
Only Chip variant=advanced opens a Popover.

input.title: Input fields
input.purpose: Collect a single value from the user. All fields share Label → Field → Help-Text anatomy and the Leading/Trailing slots.
use: Free text → InputField; long text → TextAreaField.
One option from a list → SelectField (≤ 10 options), otherwise AutocompleteField.
Dates → DateField; quantities → NumberField (steppers).
Inline editable titles → HeadingField.
avoid: 2–5 mutually exclusive visible options → RadioButton group or Segmented.
do: Always render a visible label; use aria-label only when the context already labels the field (e.g. a Share link row).
Validate on blur or submit, then show error text that says how to fix it.
Use Read-only for values the user may see but not change.
Make a labelled Leading/Trailing slot a picker (options) for units, country codes or account types.
Clamp NumberField with min/max; steppers disable at the bounds.
Keep help text to one line; move long guidance to InputConditions or docs.
dont: Don't use Disabled on inputs; Zen inputs have Read-only only (Search is the exception).
Don't use placeholder text as the label.
Don't show an error before the user has interacted with the field.
Don't give an icon-only Leading/Trailing slot click behaviour; clicks focus the field.
Don't open a Date/Select popover on a read-only field.
a11y: The whole field is the click target (padding/icons focus the native field; Select opens).
Errors set aria-invalid and link the message via aria-describedby.
NumberField is role=spinbutton: ↑/↓ step, Enter/blur clamp.
Select and Date pickers: ↓ opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.
content: Labels are nouns ("Work email"); errors are sentences with the fix ("Enter a valid email address, like name@company.com").

rules.summary: Inputs use Read-only, never Disabled (Search is the only exception).
Every field has a visible label (or an aria-label when the context labels it).

search.title: Search
search.purpose: Find or filter content by typing. The only input with a Disabled state.
use: Filtering a visible list or table as the user types.
Global/entity search with results below.
avoid: Picking from a known short list → SelectField or a Chip filter.
do: Describe the scope in the placeholder ("Search components").
Filter live and show an empty state that echoes the query.
Let Enter open the first result; the clear button resets to recent items.
Pair Search with Chip filters in table toolbars.
dont: Don't hide search behind an icon on desktop when search is a primary task.
Don't clear the query when results update.
a11y: type=search; aria-label defaults to the placeholder.
Announce result counts with aria-live.

rules.summary: Search needs a placeholder that says what is searched, or an aria-label.

segmented.title: Segmented
segmented.purpose: Switch between 2–5 mutually exclusive views or sections of the same content.
use: View switchers (grid ↔ list).
Section switchers with counters (Inbox · Mentions).
avoid: More than 5 options or long labels → Tabs or SelectField.
do: Name the control with aria-label.
Keep labels to one or two words; icon-only items still need a label for assistive tech.
Use badges for counts and hide them at zero.
Keep the selected segment static: no hover and a default cursor, because one option is always selected and re-clicking it does nothing.
dont: Don't use Segmented as a filter.
Don't mix icon-only and labelled items in one control.
Don't add a hover or pressed state to the selected segment; it suggests the choice can be undone by clicking it again.
a11y: Radiogroup semantics; arrow keys move the selection.

rules.summary: Segmented needs an aria-label naming what it switches.

toggle.title: Toggle
toggle.purpose: Turn a setting on or off with immediate effect.
use: Settings that apply instantly (notifications, dark preview).
avoid: Choices that need a Save/Submit → Checkbox.
Mutually exclusive options → RadioButton or Segmented.
do: Apply the change immediately; no confirm button.
Use a master toggle to disable dependent toggles, and explain in its caption.
Label the setting, not the state ("Email notifications", not "On").
dont: Don't use a Toggle inside a form that is submitted later.
Don't add a forced hover state; real hover is built in.
a11y: role=switch semantics via the native checkbox; Space toggles.
The label and caption are part of the clickable area.
content: Positive phrasing; avoid double negatives ("Hide inactive" → "Show inactive").

rules.summary: Checkbox, Radio and Toggle always carry a label.

checkbox.title: Checkbox
checkbox.purpose: Select zero, one or many independent options, or confirm a single statement.
use: Multi-select lists, select-all with indeterminate parent.
Consent that gates a primary action.
do: Always give a label; clicking the label toggles.
Use indeterminate only for a parent whose children are partially selected; clicking resolves it.
Explain disabled options in the caption ("Unavailable on the Free plan").
dont: Don't use a checkbox for an action that happens immediately.
Don't pre-check consent boxes for marketing.
a11y: Native checkbox; Space toggles; aria-checked=mixed for indeterminate.

rules.summary: Checkbox, Radio and Toggle always carry a label.

radio-button.title: Radio Button
radio-button.purpose: Pick exactly one option from a small visible set.
use: 2–6 options that benefit from being compared side by side (plans, density).
do: Wrap radios in role=radiogroup with an aria-label, and share one name.
Pre-select the recommended option when there is a safe default.
Use captions for price or consequence.
dont: Don't render a lone radio; it cannot be unselected.
Don't use radios for independent choices.
a11y: Arrow keys move and select within the group; Tab enters/leaves the group.

rules.summary: Checkbox, Radio and Toggle always carry a label.
Radios share a name so arrow keys move within one group.

badge.title: Badge & Badge-Counter
badge.purpose: Non-interactive status, category or count labels.
use: Status in lists (Live, Failed).
Unread/notification counts (BadgeCounter).
Removable labels on an item (remove + onRemove).
do: Map status to semantic themes consistently (green = success, red = failure, yellow = attention).
Use Subtle backgrounds in dense tables and Solid for emphasis.
Cap counters at "99+" and hide them at zero.
dont: Don't make a badge clickable (use Chip).
Don't rely on colour alone; keep the text.
a11y: The remove button is labelled ("Remove <label>").
content: One or two words; no punctuation.

rules.summary: A remove affordance must be wired to onRemove.
Counters cap at 99+.

tag.title: Tag
tag.purpose: A chosen value inside a field (keywords, recipients), usually removable.
use: Autocomplete selections, keyword inputs.
do: Let Backspace in an empty field remove the last tag.
Flag invalid values with error and explain in the field's error text.
dont: Don't use tags as buttons.
a11y: The remove button is named "Remove <value>".
content: Show the value exactly as entered.

rules.summary: A remove affordance must be wired to onRemove.

avatar.title: Avatar & Avatar Stack
avatar.purpose: Represent a person or workspace with a photo or initials.
use: People lists, assignees, account switchers, shared-with stacks (max 5).
do: Set alt to the person's name; use alt="" only when the name is shown next to the avatar.
Use 2 initials (1 on xsmall/2xsmall).
Use square avatars for workspaces and organisations.
In captioned Popover items use Avatar Small (32px) or larger (enforced by PopoverItem).
dont: Don't show more than 5 avatars in a stack; summarise the rest in text.
Don't use status without a text equivalent nearby ("Online").
a11y: Status dot has aria-label "Online".

rules.summary: Avatars need alt (the person's name; alt="" only when the name is shown next to it).

popover.title: Popover
popover.purpose: The shared floating list used by Chip, Select, Autocomplete and Leading/Trailing pickers.
use: Option lists (single or multiple), sort menus, assignee pickers with search.
avoid: Rich interactive content or forms → Dialog.
do: Pass images via photoSrc; the item renders the Figma size for its theme.
Use Avatar Small (32px) or larger when an item has a caption.
Give it anchorRef + onOpenChange so outside-click and Escape close it and focus returns.
Keep single-select popovers closing on select; keep multi-select open.
Offer Manual-Add-New (onPopoverCreate / onCreate) when users may need a value that isn't listed, e.g. labels, tags or keywords. The Create row appears only for a new value, and Enter creates it.
dont: Don't pass your own sized / as leading for avatar/photo themes.
Don't put buttons or inputs (other than the Search row) inside items.
Don't dead-end a searchable list with "No results" when creating the value is allowed; use Manual-Add-New.
Don't offer Create for closed sets (statuses, roles, countries).
a11y: role=listbox / option with aria-selected; ↑/↓/Home/End move; Escape closes and restores focus.
content: Label = category; item label = value; caption = secondary fact.

rules.summary: A controlled Popover needs onOpenChange so outside-click and Escape can close it.

sidebar.title: Sidebar
sidebar.purpose: Primary app navigation with sections, nested items and a collapsible rail.
use: App shells with 5+ destinations.
avoid: Actions → Buttons in the page header.
do: Move selection with onItemClick; exactly one selected item.
Group items under short section titles.
Use counters for actionable counts; notification dots for "something new".
dont: Don't force hover/focus states in examples; use real interaction.
Don't nest more than one level.
a11y: aria-current=page on the selected item; collapsed items keep aria-label/title.

date-picker.title: Date Picker
date-picker.purpose: Pick a date or a date range.
use: DateField in forms; inline DatePicker for booking-style range selection.
avoid: Known far-past dates (birthdays) → typed DateField without calendar-first UX.
do: Disable impossible dates (past check-in) with minDate.
Show the chosen range and its consequence (nights, price) next to the calendar.
dont: Don't open the calendar for read-only DateFields.
a11y: Nav buttons are labelled; days are buttons with the date in the label.
content: Use the locale's date format in the field placeholder.

rules.summary: Inputs use Read-only, never Disabled (Search is the only exception).
Every field has a visible label (or an aria-label when the context labels it).

tooltip.title: Tooltip
tooltip.purpose: Name or briefly describe a control on hover and keyboard focus.
use: Icon-only buttons, truncated text, keyboard shortcuts.
avoid: Essential information or anything interactive → Popover or inline help.
do: Wrap a focusable trigger (Button, IconButton, link).
Keep text under ~80 characters, no punctuation for single phrases.
Use Accent briefly for confirmations ("Copied!").
dont: Don't put links or buttons inside a tooltip.
Don't repeat the visible label word for word.
a11y: role=tooltip linked with aria-describedby; Escape dismisses; appears on focus.

rules.summary: Tooltips wrap a focusable element so keyboard users can reach them.
Tooltip text stays under ~80 characters and holds no interactive content.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.purpose: Switch between related panels of content at the same level.
use: Settings pages, detail views with sections (Indicator).
Compact switches inside cards (Subtle, small).
do: Give the tablist an aria-label and pair each tab with a TabPanel.
Keep 2–7 tabs with short labels.
Show counts with badges; hide at zero.
dont: Don't use tabs to submit or navigate away.
Don't mix icon-only and labelled tabs.
a11y: Roving tabindex; ←/→ select, Home/End jump, disabled tabs are skipped.

rules.summary: A tablist needs an aria-label.

breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.purpose: Show where the current page sits in a hierarchy and let users go up.
use: Pages 3+ levels deep; file browsers.
do: Make the last item the current page (not a link).
Collapse long paths with maxItems.
Use the same labels as page titles.
dont: Don't use breadcrumbs as the only navigation.
Don't change the icon colour on hover (the wrapper turns Inverse/Solid, the icon stays Neutral/Strongest).
a11y: nav aria-label="Breadcrumb" + ordered list; aria-current=page.

progress.title: Progress
progress.purpose: Show determinate progress of a task or a step.
use: Uploads, setup checklists, quotas (Status theme).
avoid: Unknown duration → Skeleton or a spinner.
do: Label every progress (visible label or aria-label).
Use Status only when low values are a problem (quotas, health).
Switch to Status/green or Done when complete.
dont: Don't animate backwards.
Don't use colour alone to convey state.
a11y: role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max and valuetext.

rules.summary: Progress needs a visible label or an aria-label.

dialog.title: Modal & Dialog
dialog.purpose: Interrupt to confirm a decision or deliver critical information.
use: Destructive confirmations, unsaved-changes guards, blocking success/failure.
avoid: Long forms → a page or Side Panel.
do: Phrase the title as the question ("Delete “Marketing site”?") and repeat the verb in the primary action.
Use theme negative + level danger for irreversible actions; give Cancel initial focus.
Require typing the name for high-impact deletes.
dont: Don't stack dialogs.
Don't use a dialog for information the user can ignore.
Don't hide the only way out (always Escape or a cancel action).
a11y: role=dialog/alertdialog, aria-modal, labelled by the title; focus is trapped and restored to the opener.
content: Title ≤ 1 line; description states the consequence.

rules.summary: Dialogs always have a title.
A negative (destructive) dialog's primary action uses level danger.

icon.title: Icon
icon.purpose: Render a system icon from the generated set at a token size.
use: Inside components' icon slots and next to text.
avoid: Illustrations or brand logos at large sizes.
do: Use line icons by default and solid for selected/filled states and remove affordances (icon-x-circle-solid).
Mark icons decorative when a text label is present.
dont: Don't use an icon alone as the only label of an action without aria-label.
a11y: Decorative icons are aria-hidden; meaningful icons need a text alternative.
